mainTopic: Mixtures: assuming the lost item was the forbidden one, fixing barrels of תרומה, how a טריפה gets mixed in, and סמיכה in mixed-up קרבנות
overview: The גמרא first explains that a ברייתא's 'three' items means two permitted items plus the doubtful one that fell in, so a simple majority is enough. It then offers a second source for שמואל's strict view: he follows רבי אליעזר. ריש לקיש rules that if a barrel of תרומה is mixed with a hundred barrels and one barrel falls into ים המלח, the rest are permitted, because we assume the forbidden one fell. The גמרא explains why both this ruling and רב נחמן's ruling about rings of עבודה זרה are needed. רבה and רב יוסף then argue whether ריש לקיש's rule also works for a fig. רבי אלעזר, as reworded by רב נחמן, and רבי אושעיא teach how an opened barrel in a mixture of תרומה can be fixed, while closed barrels stay forbidden. Next, the גמרא asks how a טריפה can be mixed in with קרבנות without being recognized. רבי ינאי's school, ריש לקיש and רבי ירמיה each give a different case, and the גמרא explains why each rejects the others' answers. Finally, the גמרא asks how mixed-up קרבנות can be offered when each one needs סמיכה. רב יוסף limits the משנה to women's קרבנות, and the גמרא begins to question that answer.

steps.title: Why three? Two is already a majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs the item to fall into three others, since even two permitted items would already be a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about three, that there is a majority? With two there is also a majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning a detail in the ברייתא it just quoted. If the whole point is having a majority of permitted items, why did the ברייתא say 'three'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on a majority (רוב) cancelling out the doubtful item. If one doubtful item lands among two permitted ones, the permitted already outnumber it two to one. So the number 'three' looks like more than is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case special?
A majority
Also, too

phrases.english: What is different about three,
that there is a majority?
phrases.notes: He means: is the reason for three just so that the permitted items are the majority?

phrases.english: With two there is also a majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא cited just before this section and questions its number.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's requirement that the item fall into three others
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A majority already exists with two permitted items, so 'three' seems to be more than needed.

steps.title: Three means two plus the one that fell in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'three' counts the two permitted items together with the doubtful item that fell into them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'three' that it teaches? Two, and it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The ברייתא never needed three permitted items; 'three' is the total after the doubtful item joins two permitted ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed 'three' meant three permitted items plus the one that fell in. The answer reads it as a total count of two permitted plus the one doubtful item. So the ברייתא really does agree that two permitted items are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: That it teaches (in the ברייתא)
Two
And it (the item itself)

phrases.english: What is the 'three' that it teaches?
Two, and it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the doubtful item that fell in, which makes three all together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the number in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Three' means three permitted items besides the one that fell in.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Three' is the total: two permitted items plus the doubtful one.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, 'three' means two permitted items plus the one that fell in, so a simple majority is enough.

steps.title: Another answer: שמואל follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the question of whose view שמואל follows in being strict about עבודה זרה, and offers another answer: he follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: he holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier question about which תנא שמואל follows, and gives a second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer tied שמואל to the ברייתא just discussed. This second answer instead links him to רבי אליעזר, who is also strict about mixtures that contain items of עבודה זרה. Either way, שמואל's strict ruling has a תנא behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (an alternative answer)
He holds in accordance with...

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
He holds like רבי אליעזר.
phrases.notes: 'He' is שמואל, from the discussion just before this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about 'three' and returns to the main question of whom שמואל follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a different תנא who supports the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's strict view needs the ברייתא as its source.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל could simply follow רבי אליעזר, who is strict about mixtures of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to find a source for שמואל's strict view: the ברייתא, or רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: if one barrel is lost, assume it was the תרומה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that if a barrel of תרומה was mixed with a hundred barrels and one barrel fell into ים המלח, all the remaining barrels are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: A barrel of תרומה that got mixed with one hundred barrels, and one of them fell into ים המלח, all of them become permitted, because we say: the one that fell, it was the forbidden one that fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from ריש לקיש on a related topic. When one barrel from a mixture is lost, we assume it was the forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the barrel fell, the whole group was treated as תרומה because the תרומה barrel could not be identified. Once one barrel is lost for good, we may assume the lost one was the תרומה barrel. So everything left counts as ordinary permitted produce. This is the same idea as רב נחמן's ruling about the rings of עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel
The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים
That became mixed
The Dead Sea
All of them became permitted
The forbidden item

phrases.english: ריש לקיש says:
A barrel of תרומה
that got mixed in with one hundred barrels,
and one of them fell into ים המלח,
all of them become permitted;
because we say: that one which fell,
it was the forbidden one that fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related ruling that matches רב נחמן's earlier rule about rings of עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one barrel falls out of a mixture holding one תרומה barrel, we assume the תרומה barrel fell, and all the rest are permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the barrels became permitted by being outnumbered. The mixture stayed forbidden until a barrel was lost; it is permitted only because we assume the lost barrel was the forbidden one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the 'one that fell was the forbidden one' rule as working beyond עבודה זרה, which the next step discusses.

steps.title: Why we need both רב נחמן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why both rulings were needed: from רב נחמן alone, we might have limited the rule to עבודה זרה, which has no way to be permitted, and not applied it to תרומה, which does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן's ruling was needed, and ריש לקיש's ruling was needed. For if we had only רב נחמן's, I would have said: this applies only to עבודה זרה, which has nothing that can permit it; but תרומה, which has something that can permit it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it needs two rulings that look so alike. This step gives the first half: what we would have mistakenly thought with only רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item of עבודה זרה can never become permitted, so there is good reason to be lenient and assume it was the one that fell. A mixture of תרומה does have a way out (it can be given to כהנים), so we might have said there is no need to rely on the 'it fell' assumption. ריש לקיש's ruling teaches that the rule applies to תרומה too. The next step gives the other half of this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was needed
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
This applies only...
Things that can permit it, ways for it to become allowed

phrases.english: And רב נחמן's ruling was needed,
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן's ruling about a ring of עבודה זרה mixed with other rings, quoted earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: and ריש לקיש's ruling was needed;
for if we had only רב נחמן's, I would have said:
this applies only to עבודה זרה,
which has nothing that can permit it;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תְּרוּמָה דְּיֵשׁ לָהּ מַתִּירִין – לָא.
phrases.english: but תרומה, which has something that can permit it, no.
phrases.notes: A mixture of תרומה can still be used, because it can go to כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּרַב נַחְמָן וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why ריש לקיש's ruling in step 4 is not just a repeat of רב נחמן's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן's ruling alone might have been limited to עבודה זרה, which can never become permitted; ריש לקיש teaches that the rule also covers תרומה.

steps.title: Why we also need רב נחמן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: If we had only ריש לקיש's ruling, we might limit it to a barrel, whose falling is noticeable, and not apply it to a ring. So both rulings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had learned only from ריש לקיש, I would have said: a barrel is different, because people notice when it falls; but a ring, whose falling is not noticed, would not be permitted. So both rulings are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it started in Step 5. It shows what we would have gotten wrong if we had only ריש לקיש's ruling, and concludes that both rulings are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a big barrel falls into the sea, everyone sees it, so nobody will think mixtures get permitted for no reason. A small ring falling away is not noticed, so we might have been strict there. רב נחמן's ruling teaches that even a ring counts.

keyTerms.meaning: noticeable, easy to see
a ring
both are needed; neither ruling can be learned from the other

steps.whatToRemember: Each ruling teaches something the other could not. רב נחמן shows the rule works even for something unnoticeable, like a ring. ריש לקיש shows it works even for something that has a way to be permitted, like תרומה.

phrases.english: And if from Reish Lakish, I would have said:
a barrel, whose falling is noticeable;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל טַבַּעַת, דְּלָא מִינַּכְרָא נְפִילָתָהּ – לָא.
phrases.english: but a ring, whose falling is not noticeable, no.
phrases.notes: This is the ring of עבודה זרה from רב נחמן's case.

phrases.english: Both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the explanation of why both rulings are needed, which began in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are needed, because each one covers a case the other would have left open.

steps.title: רבה limits ריש לקיש to a barrel, not a fig
steps.stepSummary: רבה says ריש לקיש permitted the rest only when a barrel fell, because that is noticeable, but not when a fig fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: ריש לקיש permitted the rest only in the case of a barrel, because its falling is noticeable. A fig, though, is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains how far ריש לקיש's leniency goes. He says it only works for a big item like a barrel, not a small item like a fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה picks up on the reason just given: a barrel's fall is noticeable. A single fig dropping out of a pile is not noticed, so in his view the rest of the figs stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a fig
falling

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Reish Lakish did not permit
except a barrel, whose falling is noticeable;
but a fig, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לֹא הִתִּיר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֶלָּא חָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'noticeable falling' reason from Step 6 to set a limit on ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's leniency applies only to a large item whose fall is noticeable, like a barrel, and not to a fig.

steps.title: רב יוסף says even a fig counts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees. Even with a fig, just as one falling in made the mix forbidden, one coming out makes it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: even a fig. Just as its falling in worked, so does its coming out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with רבה and says ריש לקיש's leniency also covers a fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not care whether people notice. His logic is about balance: one fig was enough to make the whole pile a doubtful mixture, so one fig leaving is enough to remove the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: coming up, coming out (of the mixture)
its coming out works just like its falling in

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: even a fig,
like its falling, so is its coming up.
phrases.notes: One fig falling in made the pile a problem, so one fig coming out fixes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה's limit from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's leniency applies even to a fig, because removing one item works the same way as adding one.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: open one barrel, take out the amount, and drink
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that when a barrel of תרומה falls among a hundred barrels, one opens one of them, takes out the amount of the תרומה, and drinks the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: if a barrel of תרומה fell among a hundred barrels, he opens one of them, takes out of it the amount needed for the mixture, and drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר about a barrel of תרומה that got mixed in with a hundred ordinary barrels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sealed barrels are treated as important, so they do not simply cancel out in the mixture. Opening one barrel lets it be handled like a normal mixture. Its proportional share of תרומה (about one-hundredth) is taken out and given to a כהן, and the rest of that barrel may be drunk.

keyTerms.meaning: a mixture of תרומה with ordinary food; here, the amount taken out because of it
the portion given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
a barrel of teruma
that fell among a hundred barrels,
he opens one of them
and takes from it the amount of its mixture,
phrases.notes: He takes out only this barrel's share of the תרומה, about one part in a hundred, and gives that to a כהן.

phrases.english: and drinks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה בְּמֵאָה חָבִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related ruling about a barrel of תרומה mixed among barrels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Open one barrel, remove the amount of the תרומה, and the rest may be drunk.

steps.title: רב נחמן objects: this sounds like opening a barrel on purpose
steps.stepSummary: When רב דימי taught רבי אלעזר's ruling, רב נחמן objected that it sounds like you may open a barrel and drink right from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי was sitting and teaching this ruling. רב נחמן said to him: what I see here is 'gulp and drink'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the wording of רבי אלעזר's ruling as רב דימי taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he opens one of them' sound like an instruction to open a barrel on purpose just so you can drink. רב נחמן finds it hard to accept that this is allowed from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching, a ruling
gulp and drink, meaning to go ahead and drink right away

phrases.english: Rav Dimi was sitting
and saying this teaching,
Rav Nachman said to him:
"Gulp and drink" is what I see here!
phrases.notes: He means the wording makes it sound like you may open a barrel on purpose and drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי אלעזר's ruling from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'he opens one of them' in רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It sounds like an instruction to open a barrel on purpose, from the start, which should not be allowed.

steps.title: Reworded: only if a barrel already got opened
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rewords the ruling: if one of the barrels got opened, one takes out the amount and drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: if one of them got opened, he takes out of it the amount needed for the mixture, and drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן fixes the wording, so the ruling applies only after a barrel has already been opened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is from 'he opens' to 'it was opened'. That means you should not open a barrel on purpose. But if one already got opened, you may take out the amount of the תרומה and drink the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say; a formula for rewording a teaching
it was opened (already happened)

steps.whatToRemember: You may not open a barrel on purpose to get rid of the problem. Only if a barrel was already opened may you take out the amount of the תרומה and drink the rest.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the change from 'פּוֹתֵחַ' (he opens) to 'נִפְתְּחָה' (it was opened). That one word decides whether this is allowed from the start or only after the fact.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
if one of them got opened,
he takes from it the amount of the mixture,
and drinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's objection in Step 10 by rewording רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One may open a barrel on purpose, take out the amount, and drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only if a barrel was already opened may one take out the amount and drink; opening one on purpose is not allowed.

steps.title: Only the opened barrels can be fixed; the closed ones stay forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא: one barrel of תרומה is mixed into 150 barrels and 100 of them are opened. One takes out the amount of the תרומה and drinks the opened barrels. The other 50 stay forbidden until they are opened too, because we don't assume the forbidden barrel was in the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: A barrel of תרומה got mixed in with 150 barrels, and 100 of them were opened. One takes out the amount of the mix and drinks. The rest stay forbidden until they are opened. We do not say the forbidden barrel must be in the bigger group.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא adds a new ruling about barrels. It covers a case where only some of the barrels in the mixture were opened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 100 barrels are opened, those can be fixed by taking out the amount of the תרומה. The 50 closed barrels are not automatically allowed just because the opened group is the majority. We do not assume the תרומה barrel was among the opened ones, so the closed barrels stay forbidden until they too are opened and fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel (here, of wine)
A mixture of תרומה with ordinary food; here, the amount taken out to fix it
"The forbidden item is in the majority": an assumption the גמרא refuses to make here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that because most of the barrels were opened, the closed ones become allowed. רבי אושעיא says the opposite: the closed barrels stay forbidden until they are opened.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
A barrel of terumah
that got mixed in with one hundred and fifty barrels,
and one hundred of them were opened:
he takes from it the amount of the mixture, and drinks,
and the rest are forbidden until they are opened;
we do not say
that the forbidden one is in the majority.
phrases.notes: The "majority" here is the 100 opened barrels. We don't assume the תרומה barrel was one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב נחמן's version of רבי אלעזר's ruling (once a barrel is opened, one takes out the amount). It adds the case where only some of the barrels were opened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opened barrels may be fixed and drunk. Unopened barrels stay forbidden until opened, because we don't assume the תרומה barrel was in the opened majority.
steps.whatToRemember: Opening a barrel lets you fix that barrel. Closed barrels are not released by the majority.

steps.title: How can a טריפה be mixed in without being recognized?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of forbidden animals mixed in with קרבנות. The other animals on the list look normal, but how can a טריפה be on the list? If you can recognize it, remove it; if not, how do you know it is there?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "An animal that lay with a person, or that a person lay with, etc." Granted, all the others can't be told apart by looking. But a טריפה, what is the case? If he recognizes it, let him come and take it out! If he doesn't recognize it, how does he know it got mixed in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the list of forbidden animals mixed in with קרבנות. It challenges how a טריפה could belong on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other animals on the list, like one used for עבודה זרה, look exactly like any other animal, so a mix-up makes sense. A טריפה is defined by a physical injury, so it seems you should either see it or not know about it at all. Either way, there is no real "mixed and unknown" case.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that lay with a person, or that a person lay with
An animal with a fatal injury or defect, forbidden to eat or offer
"Granted this... but that": a formula that sets one case against another to raise a problem
What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?

phrases.english: "An animal that lay with a person, or that a person lay with, etc."
Granted, all of them cannot be recognized;
but this tereifa, what is the case?
If he recognizes it, let him come and take it out!

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא יָדַע לֵיהּ – מְנָא יָדַע דְּאִיעָרַב?
phrases.english: If he does not recognize it, how does he know that it got mixed in?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ לָא יְדִיעַ אֶלָּא הַאי טְרֵיפָה הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the barrel discussion and returns to the משנה's list of forbidden animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of a טריפה among the animals that got mixed in with קרבנות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma with two sides. If the טריפה is recognizable, just remove it and there is no mixture problem. If it isn't recognizable, there is no way to know a טריפה is there at all.

steps.title: A thorn-pierced animal mixed with a wolf-clawed one
steps.stepSummary: בי רבי ינאי answer: an animal pierced by a thorn (still kosher) got mixed with one clawed by a wolf (a טריפה). Both have similar wounds, so you know a טריפה is there but can't tell which one it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: What case are we dealing with here? Where an animal pierced by a thorn got mixed up with an animal clawed by a wolf.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי gives a case that escapes both sides of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know a טריפה is in the group because a wolf clawed one of the animals. We can't pick it out because the other animal also has a puncture wound, from a thorn, and the two wounds look alike. So the טריפה is known to be there but can't be identified.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?": introduces a narrower case that solves the problem
An animal pierced by a thorn; this does not make it a טריפה
An animal clawed by a wolf; this makes it a טריפה

phrases.english: They said in the school of Rabbi Yannai:
What are we dealing with here?
For example, where an animal pierced by a thorn got mixed up
with an animal clawed by a wolf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טריפה must be either obvious or unknown.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two animals with look-alike wounds, only one of which is a טריפה, give a case of a known but unidentifiable טריפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it was mixed with an animal that fell
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers differently: the case is an animal mixed with a נפולה, an animal that fell and might be hurt inside with no sign on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: For example, where it got mixed up with an animal that fell.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נפולה may have internal injuries that make it a טריפה, but nothing shows on the outside. Someone who saw it fall knows a possible טריפה is in the group, but afterward can't tell which animal it was.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that fell (from a height) and may have been injured inside

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
[For example,] where it got mixed up with an animal that fell.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר כְּגוֹן דְּאִיעָרַב בִּנְפוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an answer to step 13 that differs from בי רבי ינאי's answer in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different case setting for the משנה (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzMaskana: A fallen animal is a possible טריפה with no outward sign, so it can be mixed in without being identified.

steps.title: Why not just check the fallen animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: a fallen animal can be checked, so why is there a problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: A fallen animal too, let him check it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a fallen animal can be checked to see whether it was hurt, then you can clear the whole group. So it seems ריש לקיש's case doesn't really create an unresolvable mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him check it

phrases.english: A fallen animal too, let him check it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's case of a mixture with a נפולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fallen animal's status can be found out by checking it, so the doubt can be removed.

steps.title: Standing or even walking does not clear a fallen animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that a fallen animal that stood up still needs a 24-hour wait, and one that walked still needs a check. A quick look does not remove the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: if it stood up, it needs a full day; if it walked, it needs a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by explaining his view of what a fallen animal needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, even a fallen animal that gets up is not cleared right away; it needs 24 hours. Even one that walks still needs a check to see whether it was hurt. Because the animal can't be cleared on the spot, the mixture stays doubtful, and the משנה's case works.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this view)
A full 24-hour period
A check to find out if the animal was injured

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for how a טריפה gets mixed in unrecognized. בי רבי ינאי: look-alike wounds (thorn and wolf). ריש לקיש: a fallen animal, which even after standing or walking is not cleared right away.

phrases.english: He holds:
if it stood up, it needs twenty-four hours,
if it walked, it needs a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 and defends ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fallen animal can be cleared by a quick look.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש holds that a fallen animal needs a 24-hour wait or a check, so it remains a possible טריפה in the mixture.

steps.title: A third answer: mixed with the offspring of a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה means a healthy animal mixed with the offspring of a טריפה, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה says: the case is where the animal got mixed with the offspring of a טריפה. This follows רבי אליעזר, who says the offspring of a טריפה may not be offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a third way to explain how a טריפה can be in the mix without anyone knowing which animal it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offspring of a טריפה looks completely healthy, so nobody can pick it out. That solves the question from Step 13. But it only works if the offspring counts as forbidden, and that is רבי אליעזר's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring (baby) of an animal that is a טריפה
That got mixed in
Onto the altar

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says:
for example, where it got mixed with the offspring of a tereifa,
and this follows Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: the offspring of a tereifa
may not be offered on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּאִיעָרַיב בִּוְלַד טְרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of Step 13, alongside בי רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a new case that fits the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טריפה always has some sign, so it should be recognizable
steps.terutzMaskana: The offspring of a טריפה has no sign at all, and according to רבי אליעזר it is forbidden for the מזבח

steps.title: Why the others reject רבי ינאי's answer
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש and רבי ירמיה hold that a thorn hole and a wolf's claw mark can be told apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them do not explain it like רבי ינאי. The difference between a thorn wound and a wolf wound is clearly known: one is long and the other is round.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why each אמורא gave his own answer. It starts with why the others did not accept רבי ינאי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי said the two wounds look alike, so you can't tell which animal is the טריפה. The others say you can tell them apart: the wolf's wound is long and the thorn's wound is round. So in his case the טריפה could be found and removed.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them (here, the other אמוראים)
It is clearly known
Long, stretched out
Round

phrases.english: All of them do not explain it like Rabbi Yannai,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the other two: ריש לקיש and רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: because between an animal pierced by a thorn
and one clawed by a wolf, the difference is clearly known;
this one is long and that one is round.
phrases.notes: The wolf's wound is the long one, and the thorn's wound is the round one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all three answers have been given, the גמרא begins explaining why each אמורא rejects the others
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי ינאי's case as an explanation of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two wounds look different, so the טריפה can be identified

steps.title: Why the others reject ריש לקיש's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי and רבי ירמיה hold that a fallen animal that stood needs no 24-hour wait, and one that walked needs no check.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not explain it like ריש לקיש, because they hold: if the animal stood, it does not need a 24-hour wait; if it walked, it does not need a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the others did not accept ריש לקיש's answer about a fallen animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, ריש לקיש said a fallen animal stays in doubt even after it stands or walks. The others disagree. Once the animal stands or walks, the doubt is gone. So in his case you can simply watch the animals, and there is no real mix-up.

keyTerms.meaning: Because they hold
It (the fallen animal) stood up
It walked

phrases.english: They do not explain it like Reish Lakish,
phrases.notes: "They" here means רבי ינאי and רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: because they hold: if it stood,
it does not need a twenty-four-hour wait,
and if it walked, it does not need a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of three explanations of why each אמורא rejects the others
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ריש לקיש's case as an explanation of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A fallen animal that stood or walked is no longer in doubt, so no unsolvable mix-up exists

steps.title: Why the others reject רבי ירמיה's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש do not want to explain the משנה according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not explain it like רבי ירמיה, because they do not want to set the משנה according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by explaining why the others did not accept רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה's answer only works if the offspring of a טריפה is forbidden, and that is רבי אליעזר's view. The others did not want to place the משנה inside רבי אליעזר's opinion. So each of the three אמוראים has a reason for his own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not set (explain) the משנה that way

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers explain how a טריפה can be hidden among קרבנות. רבי ינאי: a thorn wound mixed with a wolf wound. ריש לקיש: a fallen animal. רבי ירמיה: the offspring of a טריפה, following רבי אליעזר. Each answer is rejected by the others for its own reason: the wounds can be told apart, a fallen animal that stood or walked is fine, and the others do not want to explain the משנה like רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: They do not explain it like Rabbi Yirmeya,
phrases.notes: "They" here means רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: because they do not set the mishna according to Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last explanation, closing the comparison of the three answers
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי ירמיה's case as an explanation of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It requires explaining the משנה according to רבי אליעזר's opinion, which the others do not want to do

steps.title: How can mixed-up animals work if each one needs סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about mixed-up קדשים of the same type and asks how this works, since each owner must do סמיכה on his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if קדשים got mixed with קדשים of the same type, each animal is brought for whoever its owner is. But each animal needs סמיכה by its owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and right away asks a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says you can bring each mixed-up animal for 'whoever owns it,' and both owners are covered. But סמיכה, leaning hands on the animal, has to be done by the real owner on his own animal. Since nobody knows which animal belongs to whom, the owner can't do סמיכה properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as קרבנות
One type with the same type (for example, an עולה with an עולה)
The owner leaning his hands on his קרבן before it is slaughtered
'But look!', a word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals with sacrificial animals, a type with its own type, etc.
But it requires placing of hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the earlier steps dealt with טריפה questions, and now the גמרא turns to the line of the משנה about mixed-up קדשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that mixed-up animals of the same type are each brought for whoever their owner is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סמיכה must be done by the real owner on his own animal, and here no owner knows which animal is his.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה is about women's קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה is talking about קרבנות belonging to women, who don't do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the משנה is talking about an offering of women.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by limiting the משנה to a case where סמיכה isn't needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women don't do סמיכה on their קרבנות. So if the mixed-up animals belong to women, the סמיכה problem never comes up, and the משנה's solution works fine.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought by women, who do not do סמיכה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: With an offering of women;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סמיכה challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is set in a case where סמיכה doesn't apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה covers every owner, including men who must do סמיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is speaking only of women's קרבנות, where there is no סמיכה.

steps.title: So for men's קרבנות the משנה's solution wouldn't work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out the troubling result of רב יוסף's answer: for men's קרבנות, there would be no fix for the mix-up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with an offering of men, it would not work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer by pointing to what it leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה only works for women because they skip סמיכה, then men's mixed-up animals would have no solution at all. That is a hard result to accept, so the answer still seems lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought by men, who must do סמיכה
'But... not?', pointing to what follows from the last answer

steps.confusionAlert: This line can be read as רב יוסף finishing his own answer ('but not with men'). Here we follow the reading that it is the גמרא pointing out a problem with his answer.

phrases.english: But with an offering of men – not?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (as the end of רב יוסף's own statement, limiting the rule to women)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of רב יוסף's answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the משנה is about women's קרבנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the solution works only where there is no סמיכה, then mixed-up קרבנות of men would have no fix at all, which is hard to accept.
